About.heading: About
About.body: I'm a fullstack developer based in Karlskrona, working mainly in Next.js, TypeScript, and PostgreSQL. I graduated from Campus Värnamo's Java & Fullstack Developer programme in May 2026, and completed two internships in the Swedish tech industry along the way. I like owning a project end to end, from a blank repository to a live VPS, including CI/CD, containerisation, and the security work most tutorials skip.
About.languages: Swedish and English, professional proficiency. Arabic, native.

items.company: CM Client — AI Condition Monitoring Dashboard
bullets: Built a WebSocket-based live feed with three explicit connection states (Live / Reconnecting / Offline), removing the silent failure mode that previously blocked operator response.
Containerised the application with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes, reaching production-level availability within the four-month placement.
Shipped bilingual EN/SV support from a single Next.js codebase, ready for two target markets with zero duplicated code.
Designed a layered architecture (repository → service → security) in Next.js 15, keeping business logic independently testable.
Built role-based access control for three roles with middleware route guards, zero unauthorised access across the test suite.
Wrote a Vitest suite covering every architectural layer, enabling safe refactoring across the four-month build.
400 HVE credits, EQF Level 5. Object-Oriented Programming with Java (pass with distinction), advanced Java development, IT security, REST APIs, agile methods, and test-driven development.
Certified occupations: Application Developer, Java Developer, System Developer, Web Developer.

dar-al-alson.tagline: A multi-tenant language institute platform, architected and shipped solo.
dar-al-alson.problem: A language institute running enrolment, CEFR-aligned exams, and multi-branch finance by hand needed one system that handles Arabic-first UX and real money without cutting corners.
dar-al-alson.architecture: Next.js 16 App Router, Prisma over PostgreSQL, HTTP-only Iron-Session cookies, Redis. Containerised with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes, running on a VPS behind PM2. Bilingual and RTL-first (Arabic/English) across every screen.
dar-al-alson.security: AES-256-GCM encryption for sensitive fields, CSP nonces, HTTP-only session cookies, and per-endpoint rate limiting. No known security issues in production.
dar-al-alson.results: CEFR-aligned adaptive placement testing, anti-cheat online exams, a multi-currency payment workflow with installment plans and refund cap controls, and a daily financial close with an approval flow across multiple branches. Backed by 1,000+ unit and integration tests in Vitest, plus Playwright end-to-end coverage.
dar-al-alson.liveNote: Live in production for a real institute. Demo access available on request.

alhambra-beauty.tagline: A dual-currency, dual-script luxury commerce platform, built the way production auth should be.
alhambra-beauty.problem: An independent luxury cosmetics brand needed a real storefront, not a page builder, serving Arabic (RTL) and English shoppers with local and international pricing side by side.
alhambra-beauty.architecture: Next.js 15, Drizzle ORM over Neon Postgres, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion for the product and interaction layer.
alhambra-beauty.security: Custom JWT auth (jose) with 15-minute access tokens and 7-day transparent refresh rotation, opt-in TOTP two-factor authentication, Argon2 password hashing, progressive IP-based rate limiting (15 minutes, then 1 hour, then a permanent block), and a strict-dynamic CSP with nonce scripts.
alhambra-beauty.results: Dual-currency pricing (SYP/USD), full RTL bilingual support, an admin console, and a try-it-live product experience.

tdr-reklam.tagline: A ground-up rebuild for a real print and signage workshop in Karlskrona.
tdr-reklam.role: Solo — architecture, backend, frontend, deployment, CI/CD
tdr-reklam.problem: A physical print shop's old site couldn't take real orders, handle refunds properly, or let customers see how a vehicle decal would actually look before they paid for it.
tdr-reklam.architecture: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Drizzle ORM over Neon Postgres (EU region), bilingual sv/en via next-intl, Stripe Checkout for card and Klarna, Upstash Redis-backed rate limiting, Resend for branded transactional email, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs a secret scan, typecheck, lint, test, and build on every push to main.
tdr-reklam.security: Argon2id password hashing with timing-safe handling of unknown emails, progressive account lockout, IDOR-safe queries scoped to the session user everywhere, magic-byte file verification instead of trusting client MIME types, path-traversal-safe file serving, Stripe webhook signature verification, GDPR-compliant erasure that anonymises every table that holds personal data, and an append-only audit log for every admin mutation.
tdr-reklam.results: A canvas-based sticker placement tool for previewing decals on a vehicle silhouette (drag, tap, draw, keyboard-nudge, true-to-scale), guest and member checkout, and an admin back office covering orders, refunds, staff roles, and sales/traffic reports with PDF export. 599 tests passing, with the CI gate enforced on every push.

cm-client.tagline: Real-time industrial monitoring for AI-powered camera detection on a conveyor belt.
cm-client.role: Frontend developer, second internship placement (team project)
cm-client.problem: Operators had no reliable signal for whether the camera-detection feed was actually live or had silently dropped, which delayed response when something went wrong on the line.
cm-client.architecture: A WebSocket-based live feed with three explicit connection states, containerised with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes, with bilingual EN/SV support built into the same Next.js codebase.
cm-client.security: Deployment hardening and high-availability delivery handled as part of the Kubernetes rollout during the placement.
cm-client.results: Eliminated the silent-failure mode that previously blocked operator response, and delivered production-level high availability within the four-month placement.
